title: Vehicle Dynamic Suspension Component Map
introduction:
Use this drawing to locate the hardware of the vehicle dynamic suspension system. The Mustang’s nose points left; the transparent body shows where the highlighted components sit, while the enlarged callouts show their shapes. Match each callout to the original Item/Description table for its name and any required quantity. I read the whole-car view for location and the inset for recognition—the inset floats beside the car for clarity, not because that part lives outside the body.

The front strut combines damping with a structural role in locating the wheel, and its surrounding coil spring supports load. The rear shock controls movement alongside the rear spring. Think of the spring as storing the bump’s energy and the damper as controlling how that energy is released; otherwise, the car would keep replaying the same bump.

The front and rear height sensors report suspension position. In this adaptive system, their changing voltage gives the VDM—vehicle dynamics control module—position information. The module combines it with vehicle-motion messages to decide the damping needed at each corner. The drawing places the VDM in the rear body area and shows the sensors near their respective suspension assemblies.

This is a location and identification reference for the illustrated system. It does not establish that every Mustang has this equipment or provide trim removal, connector access, electrical test values or a calibration procedure. Sensor replacement or disturbance can require the system’s specified calibration; use the matching service instructions before that work.
